title: Template: New Analyst Lesson Notebook Repair
goal: Repair and finalize a realistic beginner-facing data analysis lesson delivery bundle from frozen course materials, structured metric definitions, quiz diagnostics, and draft teaching assets, then emit a consistent manifest, source map, instructor guide, and final package.
skillBenefitRationale: The bound skill standardizes the highest-cost checks in multi-artifact lesson tasks: notebook structure, instructor-guide alignment, source-traceability, metric-definition alignment, source-map coverage, and final package build readiness. Without the skill the task remains theoretically solvable from the visible data, docs, and drafts, but the solver must manually discover cross-file inconsistencies, compute the same diagnostics from several inputs, and keep the notebook, guide, manifest, source map, and final package synchronized.
designGoals: Keep the task centered on a realistic education deliverable rather than a code-fix or app-debugging exercise.
Use a real notebook workflow with frozen source materials, raw CSV inputs, and beginner-facing explanation constraints.
Require both pedagogical structure and data-driven correctness, so the task is not reducible to a static essay or a pure analysis script.
Let verifier focus on observable outputs, execution behavior, source traceability, and cross-file consistency instead of a single implementation path.

mainTests: The required notebook, instructor guide, lesson manifest, source map, and final package all exist, parse correctly, and include the expected lesson structure.
The notebook reads the real input files, executes successfully, and produces at least three substantive code-generated results including quiz-item diagnostics.
The notebook and guide include source citations, metric explanations, a practice section, and data-driven content consistent with the frozen inputs.
The manifest and source map use the same section order as the notebook and only reference valid source files and valid metric definitions.
The visible build script succeeds and emits a final package that reflects the repaired teaching bundle rather than a hand-written placeholder.
guardrails: Protected course materials, raw CSV inputs, and metric definitions remain unchanged.
Static placeholder notebooks, pure markdown summaries, or notebooks with no substantive code execution do not pass.
Metric names in the manifest must come from the published metric definitions, and source files must come from the visible inputs.
The final package must be produced by the visible build script rather than by hand.

readmeRequirements: Summarize why this education template aligns with high-signal SkillsMP directions such as jupyter-notebook, technical-writer, lesson planning, and tutorial asset generation.
Include oracle and with/without-skill experiment results only after real runs complete.
Explain skill relevance in terms of lower diagnosis cost across notebook structure, evidence traceability, metric-definition checks, and final notebook-manifest consistency.
